---
title: "Quickstart"
---

Harvest one collection end to end. This example takes the School of Engineering and
Natural Sciences at the University of Iceland, handle `1946/2064`.

## 1. Create the database

```bash
duckdb thesis.db < scripts/create_thesis_db.sql
```

## 2. What exists

One year at a time.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Bash

```bash
for year in $(seq 2010 2026); do
  skemman simple-search --location 1946/2064 --year "$year" --output thesis.db
done
```

## PowerShell

```powershell
foreach ($year in 2010..2026) {
  skemman simple-search --location 1946/2064 --year $year --output thesis.db
}
```

:::

This fills `thesis`: one row per search result, with the id, date, title and authors.

## 3. The item pages

```bash
skemman metadata-load --db thesis.db
```

Fetches each item page once and parses it into `thesis_metadata`, `people`,
`thesis_people`, `keywords` and `thesis_keywords`. The HTML is cached, so this is the only
time each page is fetched.

## 4. What is attached

```bash
skemman files-index --db thesis.db
```

No network at all — it reads the file table off the HTML step 3 already saved, into
`thesis_file`: filename, size, access status and type.

Run this **before** step 5. It is what lets the harvester skip closed files and take small
ones first.

## 5. The title pages

```bash
skemman titlepage-load --db thesis.db --degree-level master
```

Fetches each open PDF, keeps its first pages as text, and reads the faculty, credits and
degree into `thesis_titlepage`.

Expect roughly 25 theses a minute at the default two-second delay.

## Then query it

```sql
select faculty, count(*) as n, median(n_pages) as pages, median(ects) as ects
from thesis_titlepage
where faculty is not null
group by 1
order by 2 desc;
```
